key_facts: Catering group Compass Group plans to switch its primary stock market listing from the UK (London Stock Exchange) to the US; an official announcement is expected with its full-year results on Tuesday, according to a source close to the company cited by BBC. North America accounts for two-thirds of Compass's business, which drove its total 2025 revenues to $46.1bn. The company is expected to retain a secondary listing in London, and a consultation process with investors could take more than a year. No impact on the number of UK employees is expected.

Compass changed the currency in which it trades its standard shares on the LSE from sterling to US dollars in April of this year. In 2025 there were 23 IPOs on the London market raising £2.1bn, versus 354 IPOs raising $44bn (£33bn) in the US.

key_facts: Shares in outsourcing business Capita sank 70% after its chief executive Adolfo Hernandez stepped down with "immediate effect"; he will be replaced by current CFO Pablo Andres. Hernandez admitted the company had "not delivered" for members of the UK Civil Service pension scheme, which manages the pensions of 1.7 million public sector workers.

Capita cut its profit forecast: it now expects its 2027 underlying operating profit to be hit by £85m–£95m (previously up to £40m), due to the extra cost of the recovery plan and the loss of two other "major" contracts in the defence and pension solutions divisions. Capita plans a £190m equity raise in the first half of next year.

Capita took over administration of the Civil Service Pension Scheme from MyCSP on 1 December (2025) under a seven-year deal worth £239m; tens of thousands of retiring civil servants faced delays in receiving pension payments, and a Cabinet Office minister labelled Capita's progress "abysmal" last month.

Russ Mould of AJ Bell said Capita inherited a large case backlog and failed to deliver the promised automation, AI and digital tools; government deadlines were missed, milestone payments were withheld, and the National Audit Office is probing the contract.
importance_reason: Sharp share price collapse and CEO exit at a listed UK outsourcer with a material profit downgrade, but the effect is largely company-specific rather than systemic.
market_link: Profit downgrade and planned £190m equity raise could pressure Capita's share price and dilute existing shareholders; contract losses may weigh on sector sentiment for UK government outsourcing.

key_facts: South East Water reported a pre-tax loss of £22.9m for the six months to 30 September, compared with a profit of £18.2m in the same period last year.
The losses follow penalties and £29m of costs for responding to water supply disruption over the summer; the company set aside £14.6m in its latest results to cover a redress package.

In July, regulator Ofwat ordered the company to spend £30.5m on improvements after supply interruptions affected more than 286,000 customers in Kent and Sussex. In October the company asked shareholders for £50m, after warning it needed additional funding to stay afloat.

Chief executive David Hinton and chair Chris Train stepped down earlier in the year after MPs said they had "no confidence" in leadership; John Halsall was appointed chief executive. Richard Morse is due to become chair on 3 December, succeeding interim chair Lisa Clement.
